meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's zero, and I want to know who decided it.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
Eleven fifty-two. Eleven fifty-eight. Students draft in another program and paste it in, so what makes this more than that? I'll want that history on paper.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
Give me the text. A wrong quotation is a student's mistake, and it doesn't tell me who wrote the essay. I'll search it myself, and then I want to know where else you've looked.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Okay. I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, Thursday at 8:15, with no other students in the room. I want it in an email tonight that the zero comes off the gradebook now, the new mark goes in before his December 1 deadline, and nothing goes on his record.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a supervised rewrite of Owen's essay on Thursday at 8:15 in your room with the vice-principal supervising, its mark replacing the zero and nothing going on his record. I still require confirmation that the zero comes off the gradebook now, that the new mark is entered before his December 1 deadline, and that no other students are in the room. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and accepted a private supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook now, the new mark in before December 1, and written confirmation, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her, then gave her dated, specific things she could check herself, the document's edit times and a line she could search in the play.
What cost ground: Nothing; you never leaned on the detector score or accused Owen, so she had little to push back against.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your edit times after 11 PM the night before the due date came very close to that night, which proves nothing about the essay and is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked about the gradebook and his December 1 deadline, answer both aloud before she leaves, so the deal doesn't rest on an email she has to chase.
